item.title: Correction · Mission Rock Block J: The Port Commission approved Resolution 26-34 (up to $10…
item.description: The Port Commission approved Resolution 26-34 (up to $10 million for Phase 2 pre-development) on June 9, 2026. The Port's June 2026 report does not name this block, and no source read says which phase includes it. The Port's January 2018 staff report describes the DDA's outside dates for starting later phases (a legal deadline, not a forecast); the DDA text itself has not been read, so no calendar date is given. The Port's June 2026 report schedules the Developer's Phase 2 Submittal for Winter/Spring 2027 and a possible construction start for Summer/Fall 2027 (expected dates); no source read reports construction or a vertical design submittal for this block or states its current use. DDA-specific section numbers and target dates previously listed here are removed because the DDA text has not been read. Source: https://www.sfport.com/media/11337/download?inline https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-06/item_11a_mission_rock_phase_2_update_and_port_capital.pdf https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Mission%20Rock%20Approvals%20Staff%20Report%201-26-18FINAL.pdf https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2021-07/Mission%20Rock%20Fact%20Sheet_24June2021.pdf.

item.title: Correction · Mission Rock Block J: Block J's page now says that two of the lot lines its shape was…
item.description: Block J's page now says that two of the lot lines its shape was snapped to (the Exposition Street lot 8719A010 and lot 8719D001) carry a recorded drop date of March 18, 2025 in the Assessor data while still flagged active; the dataset does not say why. The page also now says which Phase 1 lot-to-building pairings have a source: Verde (8719C001, 1070 Bridgeview Way) does; the Visa building (8719A008), The Canyon and Building B rest on position and area. Source: DataSF Parcels - Active and Retired (acdm-wktn), https://data.sf.gov/resource/acdm-wktn.json?block_num=8719A.

item.title: Correction · Mission Rock Block J: Corrections to Block J: the Design Controls are now called a…
item.description: Corrections to Block J: the Design Controls are now called a document dated April 24, 2018. The base-building height fact now gives 60 ft with a 40 ft maximum along the Terry A. Francois Boulevard side, not 40 ft alone. The phase-status fact no longer presents the 2023 deceleration as the current state; it adds the June 2026 request to accelerate Phase 2. The Design Controls approval milestone now cites the Sep 2019 Port memo that gives the Jan 30, 2018 date and notes the memo numbers that resolution 18-05 while the January 26 staff report requested it as 18-04. The Board of Supervisors milestone no longer names 'Resolution 33-18' (the Port's reports call it a resolution and an ordinance; the Notice of Determination gives File No. 171286). The Oct 2023 milestone now says Port and developer staff agreed earlier in 2023 to decelerate Phase 2 and that Resolution 23-46's recitals state it, rather than a Commission finding on Oct 10; the March 2025 milestone quotes the memo's words and calls the 132 BMR-unit cut a proposal. The Draft EIR phasing milestone no longer says it was 'superseded'; it cites the Port's Oct 2023 list of Phase 1 buildings. The D4D source is retitled the March 2012 Design + Development Revised Proposal by the Giants and The Cordish Companies (a developer proposal, not the Design for Development), the Design Controls source is credited to the Port only, and the Design Controls figure credit no longer names Mission Rock Partners or an adoption date. The map notes now say no source read shows construction on the block and cite the Port's June 2026 report instead of a bare 'unbuilt'; the 'within 3%' area claim is corrected in a new dated note (lot A is about 3.3% under the 2012 table). Source: Port of San Francisco, Mission Rock Design Controls, 2018-04-24 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-07/Mission%20Rock%20Design%20Controls%204.24.18_FINAL_Reduced%20File.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 7A staff report, 2019-09-24 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/Documents/Item%207A%20Mission%20Rock%20Phase%201%20Budget%20Approval%20%28003%29.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 8B staff report, 2023-10-06 (https://www.sfport.com/files/2023-10/101023_8b_mission_rock_budget_port_capital_parcel_lease_amendment_final.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Commission Item 12A staff report, 2025-03-07 (https://sfport.com/media/10228/download?inline=031125_12a_mission_rock_revised_phase_1_submittal_-_info_and_possible_action.pdf); SF Planning, Notice of Determination, Seawall Lot 337 and Pier 48 Mixed-Use Project, 2018-03-09 (https://sfplanning.s3.amazonaws.com/sfmea/2013.0208ENV-Seawall%20Lot%20337_NOD.pdf); Port of San Francisco, Mission Rock Phase 2 update (Port Commission Item 11A), 2026-06-09 (https://www.sfport.com/sites/default/files/2026-06/item_11a_mission_rock_phase_2_update_and_port_capital.pdf).

item.title: Milestone · Mission Rock Block J: Port staff's memo for the Commission's March 11… (Mar 11, 2025)
item.description: Port staff's memo for the Commission's March 11, 2025 meeting (Item 12A, Resolution 25-17) proposes cutting Phase 1's BMR units from 161 to 132 and says later phases 'may require higher percentages of BMR units' to meet the project's 40% overall target; the Developer, Port and MOHCD are reviewing changes 'with the goal of improving the feasibility of future Phases of Mission Rock' (Mar 11, 2025). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2025-03-07.

item.title: Planned · Mission Rock Block J: Port Commission adopts Resolution 23-46 (passed… (Oct 10, 2023)
item.description: Port Commission adopts Resolution 23-46 (passed unanimously as amended); its recitals state that, because Phase 2 is 'not currently financially feasible', Port and Developer staff had 'mutually agreed earlier this year to decelerate work on Phase 2' (Oct 10, 2023). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2023-10-06; San Francisco Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2023-12-08; Port of San Francisco, 2023-10-10.
item.source: Port of San Francisco, 2023-10-06; San Francisco Board of Supervisors (Legistar), 2023-12-08; Port of San Francisco, 2023-10-10

item.title: Milestone · Mission Rock Block J: Developer sends the Port its Phase 2 Submittal… (Dec 28, 2022)
item.description: Developer sends the Port its Phase 2 Submittal (with a Garage Report submitted October 14, 2022 and a Basis of Design November 18, 2022); the budget and appraisal elements are deferred (Dec 28, 2022). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2023-10-06.

item.title: Milestone · Mission Rock Block J: Development Agreement takes effect (the Port's… (Aug 15, 2018)
item.description: Development Agreement takes effect (the Port's fact sheet lists the DA effective date as Aug. 15, 2018, with a 30-year term and 4 phases); the Planning page dates both the Development Agreement and the DDA 8/15/2018 (Aug 15, 2018). Source: SF Planning; Port of San Francisco, 2021-06-24.

item.title: Milestone · Mission Rock Block J: Board of Supervisors affirms the EIR certification… (Mar 6, 2018)
item.description: Board of Supervisors affirms the EIR certification and adopts CEQA findings (Board File No. 171286; approval date March 6, 2018 per the Notice of Determination, filed March 9, 2018) (Mar 6, 2018). Source: SF Planning, 2018-03-09; Port of San Francisco, 2023-10-06.

item.title: Milestone · Mission Rock Block J: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock DDA… (Jan 30, 2018)
item.description: Port Commission approves the Mission Rock DDA (Resolution 18-03) and the Design Controls that set this block's use and envelope; the Jan 26, 2018 staff report requested the Design Controls approval as Resolution 18-04, and the Sep 2019 Port memo dates the approvals January 30, 2018 (it numbers the Design Controls resolution 18-05) (Jan 30, 2018). Source: Port of San Francisco, 2018-01-26; Port of San Francisco, 2018-04-24; Port of San Francisco, 2019-09-20.
